Fabrication · Formlabs and MakerBot

Easy 3D Print

See what a 3D printer can really do, then pick one thing to print and keep

  • Grades 7 to 12
  • Time 1 class period, plus print time
  • Difficulty Beginner
  • Grade Optional

This one starts with a show. Mr. Krigger walks you through our printers, then shows off a few tricks: an AI that turns a flat picture into a 3D model in under a minute, twenty lines of code that become a twisted vase, and a script that grows a seashell one sphere at a time. After that it is your turn. Find a model online, design your own, or make one with AI, and bring it to Mr. Krigger. He prints it, and it is yours to keep. Work alone or team up with one or two friends.

This one is optional. Do it and it counts toward your grade. Skip it and it is marked Exempt, so it cannot hurt you. Due Friday, November 20.

What you'll learn

  • Where 3D models come from: model libraries, your own design, code, and AI
  • Why the same model might go on a different printer or in a different resin
  • How to check a model will actually print: size, thin parts, and time

Safety rules: every printer

  • Liquid resin stays off your skin. Nitrile or neoprene gloves, never latex, and safety glasses whenever resin is out.
  • Only students who passed the printer safety check wash, cure or remove supports, and only with Mr. Krigger in the room.
  • The MakerBot nozzle is about 200°C. Hands out while it moves.
  • No food or drink at the print station.
About accounts. The printers run on Mr. Krigger's accounts, so you never sign in to them. If you want your own Tripo3D or MakerWorld account, check the age rules in the Pick yours tab first.

The demo

Four ways to make a model

Goal: see what is possible. You do not have to use any of these tools, but after the demo you might want to.

ToolWhat you'll see
Tripo3D (AI)A sentence or a flat picture becomes a 3D model in under a minute. Then the catch: AI models are often too big and too thin to print, so a person still checks them.
OpenSCAD (code)A vase written as about 20 lines of code. Drag a slider for the twist or the number of points and a new vase appears.
BlenderA script grows a spiral shell from one sphere. Change one number, get more turns.
MathThe gyroid: one equation turned into a shape nobody could carve by hand.

Try it: the vase in OpenSCAD

This is the whole vase. Paste it into OpenSCAD, press F5, then change twist or points and press F5 again.

points = 7;   twist = 120;   height = 70;   flare = 1.25;

module star(n, r1, r2) {
  polygon([for (i = [0 : 2*n - 1])
    let(r = (i % 2 == 0) ? r1 : r2, a = 180 * i / n)
    [r * cos(a), r * sin(a)]]);
}
module body(grow) {
  linear_extrude(height = height, twist = twist, scale = flare, slices = 80)
    offset(r = 2 + grow) star(points, 22, 15);
}
difference() {
  body(0);
  translate([0, 0, 2.5]) body(-2);
}
Want sliders? Download twisted_vase.scad from the Examples tab, open it, and click Window, then Customizer.

Examples

Which printer, which resin?

Our Formlabs prints with two different resins, and each one is good at different things. Pick the one that fits what you are making.

Printer and materialLooks likePick it for
Formlabs, Clear V4Frosted glass off the printer. Sanded and sprayed, nearly clearThings light passes through: lamps, gems, lattices
Formlabs, Tough 2000Gray, a little bendy, very strongThings that have to work: clips, threads, gears, snap fits
MakerBot, PLAPlastic with visible layer linesBigger, simpler shapes: vases, stands, organizers
Download all examples (zip)

Clear V4: things that look like glass

Battery tealights only in the shade. Cured resin burns.

Tripo3D (AI)Type what you want, or upload a picture, and AI builds the model. Download it as an STL.13 and up, or younger with a parent's permission. Free accounts make your models public, so no photos of people

Tripo3D tip: it works best with one object on a plain background, seen straight on. The AI pictures in the laser lesson are perfect for this. Whatever Tripo gives you, check it against the next panel before you send it.

Check it will print

  • Fits in 50 mm on every side for the Formlabs, or 80 mm for the MakerBot. Bigger only with Mr. Krigger's yes
  • Prints in 2 hours or less
  • Nothing thinner than about 1 mm. Thin tails, antennae and swords snap
  • No weapons, blades, or anything that looks like one
  • File named with your section and initials, like HS-JK-easyprint.stl
Checkpoint: every box ticked, and you know which printer or resin your model goes in.

Base and Stretch

Base · everyone

One print from any source that passes the checks.

Stretch · required for HS, bonus for MS

Make it yours. Design it yourself, or make a real change to a downloaded or AI model: resize it to fit something, add your name, combine two models, or change the demo code. Say what you changed.

What you turn in

  • Your STL, the link to the model, or the picture you gave Mr. Krigger for Tripo3D
  • A photo of the finished print
  • One sentence: which printer or resin, and why it fits your model. Stretch: what you changed
  • Crews: everyone uploads their own copy and lists the crew
Already printed something for Make Something Real or your capstone? It counts here too. Upload the same files to both.

Handing it in

Upload it in Schoology

  1. Open Easy 3D Print in Schoology
  2. Click Submit Assignment, then Upload
  3. Select your file and your photo at once, type your sentence, then Submit
Do not click "Create". Create is for typing text and will not let you attach a file. Upload is the one you want.

Vocabulary

TermWhat it means
STLThe standard 3D printing file. A shape made of tiny triangles.
SlicerSoftware that cuts a model into layers. PreForm for the Formlabs, MakerBot Print for the MakerBot.
ResinThe liquid a Formlabs printer builds from. Light turns it solid.
SupportsThin struts that hold a part up while it prints, snapped off after.
WatertightA model with no holes in its surface. Printers need this.
ParametricA design controlled by numbers you can change, like the OpenSCAD vase.

Troubleshooting

My AI model is huge.
Tell Mr. Krigger the size you want. Scaling to 40 mm is one click in the slicer.
The slicer says parts are too thin or floating.
Pick a chunkier model, or thicken those parts in Tinkercad. AI models do this a lot.
The print time says 6 hours.
Make it smaller. On the Formlabs, time depends on height, so laying it flatter helps.
I cannot download from MakerWorld.
You may be under 13. Use Printables or Thingiverse, or give Mr. Krigger a picture.
My Clear print looks cloudy or yellow.
Cloudy is normal until it is sanded. Yellow usually means it cured too long, so Mr. Krigger uses the short cure for Clear.
